usdRate.sourceName: European Central Bank euro reference rate (USD)
usdRate.note: EUR 1 = USD 1.1172 on 30 October 2026, so about EUR 0.895 per US dollar; World Bank 2025 average 0.885.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Central Statistics Office (CSO), Consumer Price Index September 2026
inflation_cpi.note: CPI up 4.1% in the 12 months to September 2026 (HICP 3.8%); 3.7% in August 2026 (Trading Economics). World Bank 2025 average 2.2%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: ECB 2% medium-term target; Irish CPI 4.1% (Sep 2026) after 2.2% in 2025 (World Bank)
inflation_projection.note: Ireland uses the euro, so the ECB 2% target anchors long-run inflation, but Irish prices have run a little above the euro area, so 2.3% is used.

policy_rate.sourceName: European Central Bank, key ECB interest rates (deposit facility)
policy_rate.note: Ireland uses the euro; ECB deposit facility rate 2.50% (main refinancing 2.65%) since 16 September 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Irish banks, household overnight deposits (new business)
savings_account_rate.note: Average rate on household overnight (instant-access) deposits at Irish banks; notice and online savings accounts pay more.

fdr_3m_rate.note: ECB and Central Bank of Ireland MFI statistics publish household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year as one bucket (1.81% in August 2026); no 3-month fixed-term rate was found.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Irish banks, household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year (new business)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Bucket covers all fixed terms up to one year; interest is subject to 33% DIRT.

dps_rate.sourceName: NTMA, State Savings rates from 30 August 2026 (6-year Instalment Savings)
dps_rate.note: Government-backed 6-year monthly savings plan: 13.5% total return, 2.33% AER (assumes an average term of 5.5 years), tax-free; new issues from 30 August 2026.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Irish banks, household deposits with agreed maturity (outstanding amounts)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Average rate on all outstanding household term deposits; World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no recent figure for Ireland.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.sourceName: NTMA, State Savings rates from 30 August 2026 (5-year Savings Certificate, Issue 26)
sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Government-backed 5-year certificate: 12% total return, 2.29% AER, tax-free if held to maturity; 3-year Savings Bonds pay 1.96% and 10-year National Solidarity Bonds 2.66% AER. Also shown on statesavings.ie/our-products/5-year-savings-certificates.

tbill_91d_rate.note: The NTMA issues Irish Treasury Bills to institutional investors, but no published 3-month yield could be read (NTMA auction pages not reachable; Trading Economics shows only the 10-year yield).

tbond_5y_rate.note: No 5-year Irish government bond yield could be read: Trading Economics and worldgovernmentbonds.com pages returned no 5-year figure.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Trading Economics, Ireland 10-year government bond yield
tbond_10y_rate.note: ECB long-term (10-year) convergence yield for Ireland was 3.59% in September 2026.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Ireland income determination
tax_bank_interest.note: Deposit Interest Retention Tax (DIRT) of 33% is deducted at source and settles the income tax due; certain people (for example some aged 65+ on low incomes) can claim exemption or repayment.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: NTMA, State Savings rates announcement (17 August 2026)
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: The NTMA states that returns on the fixed-term State Savings products are tax free (no DIRT); interest on the State Savings deposit account is subject to DIRT.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Deposit Guarantee Scheme (Central Bank of Ireland), What we cover
deposit_insurance_limit.note: EUR 100,000 for eligible deposits, paid automatically; the EU-wide limit applies per depositor per bank.

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Irish banks, revolving loans, overdrafts and credit card credit to households
credit_card_rate_cap.note: Average rate on revolving loans, overdrafts and extended credit card credit combined; Ireland has no legal cap on card rates and card APRs are typically higher.

equity_return_low.sourceName: ISEQ 14,207 on 30 Oct 2026, up 19.6% in a year (Trading Economics); State Savings tax-free about 2%
equity_return_low.note: Low case: Irish shares, a small bank-heavy market, earn little more than tax-free State Savings over a long period, as after 2007.

equity_return_base.sourceName: ISEQ (Trading Economics); 5-year Savings Certificates 2.29% tax-free (State Savings)
equity_return_base.note: The ISEQ is at a record high after a strong decade, but the base is held to the tax-free safe rate of about 2% plus 3.5 points, as a diversified fund would earn.

equity_return_high.sourceName: ISEQ price index (Trading Economics); long-run global equity returns
equity_return_high.note: High case: a diversified global or euro equity fund matching long-run equity returns of about 7-8% in euros.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD 3,876/oz on 30 Oct 2026, 31% below the January 2026 high (Trading Economics)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold barely keeps up after the 2025-26 spike, with no help from the euro.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); ECB 2% inflation target
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises roughly with world inflation plus a little, and the euro is assumed stable against the dollar over the long run.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in euro terms.

fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: deposit and State Savings rates drift lower if the ECB cuts again.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: State Savings 1.96-2.29% tax-free; 1-year deposits 1.81% less 33% DIRT = 1.2%
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: a mix of tax-free State Savings products and term deposits after DIRT.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: National Solidarity Bonds 2.66% tax-free over 10 years (State Savings)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in 10-year tax-free National Solidarity Bonds at about today's rate.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The Central Bank of Ireland and Insurance Ireland do not publish an industry-wide life claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life (life assurance and mortgage protection) is widely sold, but no published premium table per EUR 1,000 of cover by age was found; broker quote tools were not used.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Public hospital in-patient care is largely free through the HSE and most private stays are paid by insurers; no official figure for a typical out-of-pocket cost of a major private stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Irish private health insurance is community-rated (same price for all ages, plus a lifetime community rating loading for late joiners) and priced per plan, not per sum insured, so no premium per EUR 100,000 of cover by age exists.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: CSO CPI September 2026: Health division +1.8% a year
goal_inflation_health.note: Measured health prices are rising below headline inflation, but private fees and health insurance premiums tend to rise faster over time, so 3% is used.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: CSO CPI September 2026: Education Services division +8.9% a year
goal_inflation_education.note: Education prices are rising far faster than headline inflation this year; 5% allows for continued fee and childcare-linked increases without assuming the current spike lasts.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Men 81.0, women 84.9 (UN WPP estimate for 2026); World Bank 2024 figure 83.0. UN WPP mid-year estimate for 2026.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years computed from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate). UN WPP mid-year estimate for 2026.

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 24.7 (2025, World Bank), 34.8 (2040) and 47.0 (2065, populationpyramid.net/ireland/2065/).

retirement_age_default.note: State Pension age is 66 for men and women; the pension can be deferred up to 70 for a higher rate. Ireland has no general statutory retirement age for private employees.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: Single Public Service Pension Scheme, scheme overview
retirement_age_government.note: Normal retirement age for Single Scheme members (public servants recruited since 2013) equals the State Pension age, currently 66, with compulsory retirement at 70; older public servants have earlier pension ages.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates fall back after ECB cuts.

retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped at the after-tax 1-year term deposit rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: State Savings Certificates 2.29% and National Solidarity Bonds 2.66%, tax-free
retirement_return_high.note: High case: a retiree ladders tax-free 5- and 10-year State Savings products.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: State Savings about 2% tax-free; ISEQ record (Trading Economics)
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: State Savings about 2% tax-free; equity base 5.5%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 5.5% and half safe fixed income at about 1.8% after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Means-tested maximum personal rate EUR 288 a week for ages 66-79 in 2026 (EUR 288 x 52 / 12 = EUR 1,248 a month); EUR 10 a week more from January 2027 (Budget 2027).

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: From 66 for men and women; means-tested (income and capital above EUR 20,000), and the claimant must meet the habitual residence condition.

gratuity_rule.note: Ireland has no statutory gratuity paid on retirement or resignation; the only statutory lump sum is redundancy pay (2 weeks' pay per year of service plus one week, weekly pay capped at EUR 600), paid only when a job is made redundant (Citizens Information, Redundancy payments).

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Citizens Information, State Pension (Contributory); Taxation of pensions
public_pension_scheme.note: PRSI-based State Pension (Contributory) from 66, maximum EUR 299.30 a week in 2026 with 2,080 contributions (40 years), minimum 520 contributions; rates rise through the annual Budget, not by a statutory index; social welfare pensions are taxable income. MyFutureFund auto-enrolment (employees 23-60) started 1 January 2026.

savings_account.note: Instant-access and notice savings accounts at banks and credit unions; interest taxed at 33% DIRT. State Savings also offers a Deposit Account.

dps.note: Government-backed: monthly payments for 12 months, then held to 6 years for a tax-free return.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: Sold by the NTMA through State Savings; also 3-year Savings Bonds and 10-year National Solidarity Bonds, all tax-free.

tbill_91d.note: Issued by the NTMA mainly to institutional investors.

tbond_5y.note: Bought through a stockbroker; interest is taxed as income.

equity_fund.localNameEn: Unit trusts, unit-linked funds and index funds (ETF)
equity_fund.note: Gains on Irish and EU-domiciled funds and unit-linked life policies are taxed by an exit tax (38% in 2026, with a deemed disposal every 8 years) rather than capital gains tax.

gold.note: Legal to buy; investment gold is exempt from VAT and gains are subject to capital gains tax.

centralBank.name: Central Bank of Ireland
centralBank.note: Part of the Eurosystem; monetary policy set by the European Central Bank.

insuranceComplaints.name: Financial Services and Pensions Ombudsman (FSPO)
insuranceComplaints.note: Free once the insurer's own complaints process has finished.

pensionScheme.name: State Pension (Contributory), Department of Social Protection

publicHealthCover.name: Health Service Executive (HSE)
publicHealthCover.note: Public hospital care for all residents; medical cards and GP visit cards are means- or age-tested.

depositInsurance.name: Deposit Guarantee Scheme (Central Bank of Ireland)
